newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Murtaza Bhutto's widow says he feared for life.
newsitem.headline: Murtaza Bhutto's widow says he feared for life.

text.p: The widow of the slain brother of Pakistan's former prime minister Benazir Bhutto told an investigating tribunal on Monday that her husband had died as a result of a conspiracy, but did not say who was behind it.
"I agree it is a conspiracy. But who has designed that?" asked Lebanese-born Ghinwa Bhutto, while testifying before a three-judge tribunal of inquiry in Karachi.
Ghinwa said her husband had feared for his life, even though his estranged sister Benazir headed the government. "He was always apprehensive that his life was in danger," she said.
Murtaza Bhutto died in a hail of police bullets in Karachi on September 20. Police say his bodyguards fired first.
Benazir Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari is in jail facing a charge of conspiring to murder Murtaza. He denies the charge.

Ghinwa criticised Benazir Bhutto for failing immediately to arrest the policemen involved in the shooting. "Instead, she kept pointing her fingers in all directions and inventing all sorts of far-fetched theories and conspiracies," she said.
Ghinwa said Benazir Bhutto had tried to victimise and intimidate her brother before his death for speaking out against the former prime minister and her husband.
"Murtaza openly criticised Benazir and Zardari who plundered the national wealth," she said.
Benazir Bhutto, due to resume her testimony before the tribunal on Tuesday, has accused President Farooq Leghari of prompting Ghinwa to implicate Zardari in a murder conspiracy.
During her testimony on Saturday, she had said Murtaza's killing was part of a conspiracy to oust her government.
Leghari, who dismissed Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, has denied her allegations that he had conspired against her.
Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) was routed in February 3 elections by Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League.
Ghinwa Bhutto contested the polls at the head of a PPP faction founded by her husband, but the party failed to win a seat in the 217-member National Assembly (lower house).
